covers: The registers of the YM2608 (OPNA): the SSG, the rhythm voices, the FM channels and the ADPCM-B channel, both banks

left_out.why: written to the rhythm block and stored; nothing reads them, and the block's sample start and end registers are out of reach here: the sample ranges are fixed at reset
written to the rhythm block and stored; nothing reads them
written to the FM block and stored; nothing decodes it
written to the FM block and stored; nothing decodes them (the OPNA has no DAC)
a write is dropped: ymfm keeps the latched frequency bits in these slots
written to the FM block and stored; nothing decodes them
written to the FM block of the second bank and stored; nothing decodes them
the second bank's copy of the per-operator frequency registers: stored, but MAME reads them for channel 2 only
a write is dropped: ymfm keeps the latched frequency bits in the matching first-bank slots

entries.name: tone period
entries.description: Tone period of voices A, B and C, 12 bits each.
entries.behaviour: Even addresses 0x00, 0x02, 0x04 hold the low 8 bits for voices A, B, C; odd addresses 0x01, 0x03, 0x05 hold bits 11 to 8 in their low 4 bits. Reads return the byte as written.

sources.cites: //     00,02,04 xxxxxxxx Tone period (fine) for channel A,B,C

against.line: //     00,02,04 xxxxxxxx Tone period (fine) for channel A,B,C

entries.name: noise period
entries.description: Period of the noise generator.
entries.behaviour: Bits 4 to 0 are the noise period (0 to 31); bits 7 to 5 are unused. Reads return the byte as written.

entries.name: mixer, I/O direction
entries.description: Tone and noise switches of the three voices and the direction of the two I/O ports.
entries.behaviour: Bits 2 to 0 switch tone off for voices C, B, A and bits 5 to 3 switch noise off (0 enables, 1 disables). Bit 6 makes I/O port A an output and bit 7 port B (0 is input). Reads return the byte as written.

entries.name: amplitude
entries.description: Volume and envelope switch of voice A, B or C.
entries.behaviour: Address 0x08 is voice A, 0x09 B, 0x0A C. Bit 4 set makes the voice follow the envelope; clear, bits 3 to 0 give a fixed level (0 to 15, with 15 as loud as the envelope's top). Reads return the byte as written.

sources.cites: //     08,09,0A ---x---- Mode: fixed(0) or variable(1) for channel A,B,C

against.line: //     08,09,0A ---x---- Mode: fixed(0) or variable(1) for channel A,B,C

entries.name: envelope period low
entries.description: Low 8 bits of the 16-bit envelope period.
entries.behaviour: 0x0C holds the high byte. The envelope takes one step each time the period counts out, so a larger value is slower. Reads return the byte as written.

entries.name: envelope period high
entries.description: High 8 bits of the 16-bit envelope period.
entries.behaviour: 0x0B holds the low byte; the period is the two bytes together. Reads return the byte as written.

entries.name: envelope shape
entries.description: Shape of the envelope the voices can follow.
entries.behaviour: Bit 3 is continue, bit 2 attack, bit 1 alternate and bit 0 hold. Every write, even of the same value, restarts the envelope at step 0. Reads return the byte as written.

entries.name: I/O ports A and B
entries.description: The two 8-bit parallel I/O ports, A at 0x0E and B at 0x0F.
entries.behaviour: 0x07 bits 6 and 7 set port A and port B as input (0) or output (1). Reading an input port calls the port read callback and returns its value; reading an output port returns the stored byte. A write always stores and calls the port write callback only for an output.

entries.name: rhythm key on, dump
entries.description: Starts or stops the six built-in rhythm voices.
entries.behaviour: Bits 5 to 0 pick channels 0 to 5 (bass drum, snare, top cymbal, high hat, tom, rim shot). With bit 7 clear each picked channel starts its sample from the ROM range fixed at reset; with bit 7 set it stops. Unpicked channels and bit 6 are ignored.

entries.name: rhythm total level
entries.description: Master level of the six rhythm voices.
entries.behaviour: Bits 5 to 0 are the total level (0 to 63, larger is louder); bits 7 to 6 are ignored. It combines with each voice's own level at 0x18 to 0x1D.

entries.name: rhythm test
entries.description: Test register of the rhythm block.
entries.behaviour: Eight bits, stored and unused by MAME.

entries.name: rhythm level, pan
entries.description: Level and output side of one rhythm voice.
entries.behaviour: 0x18 to 0x1D are channels 0 to 5. Bit 7 sends the channel to the left, bit 6 to the right (both clear is silent); bits 4 to 0 are its level (0 to 31, larger is louder) and bit 5 is ignored. A channel is silent while (31 minus level) plus (63 minus 0x11) is 63 or more.

entries.name: test
entries.description: Test register.
entries.behaviour: Eight test bits. The byte is stored and nothing in MAME reads it.

entries.name: LFO control
entries.description: LFO enable and rate.
entries.behaviour: Bit 3 turns the LFO on and bits 2 to 0 pick its rate (0 to 7). With it off the counter is held at 0: PM does nothing and AM-enabled operators still get a fixed extra attenuation.

entries.name: timer A high
entries.description: Upper 8 bits of the 10-bit timer A preset.
entries.behaviour: 0x25 holds the lower 2 bits. The timer counts 1024 minus the value, in FM sample periods, and reads the value when it starts or re-arms after an overflow, so a change while it runs applies at the next overflow.

entries.name: timer A low
entries.description: Lower 2 bits of the 10-bit timer A preset.
entries.behaviour: Bits 1 to 0 are bits 1 to 0 of the timer A value and bits 7 to 2 are ignored; 0x24 holds the upper 8 bits.

entries.name: timer B
entries.description: Timer B preset.
entries.behaviour: All 8 bits are the value. The timer counts 16 times (256 minus the value) FM sample periods and reads the value when it starts or re-arms after an overflow.

entries.name: timer control, mode
entries.description: Timer start, flag reset and flag enable bits, and the channel 2 mode.
entries.behaviour: Bits 7 to 6: 0 normal, 1 or 3 per-operator frequencies on channel 2 (0xA8 to 0xAF), 2 also CSM (each timer A overflow keys channel 2 on); bits 5, 4 clear flags B, A; bits 3, 2 let flags B, A set and raise the interrupt; bits 1, 0 start timers B, A, and clearing one stops it.

entries.name: key on/off
entries.description: Starts or releases the operators of one channel.
entries.behaviour: Bits 7 to 4 key operators 4 to 1 on or off. Bits 1 to 0 pick the channel and bit 2 adds 3, so 0 to 2 and 4 to 6 are valid; values 3 and 7 are ignored. Operator 2 is at offset 8 in the rows from 0x30.

entries.name: interrupt enable, mode
entries.description: Chooses which status flags raise the interrupt and whether FM channels 4 to 6 sound.
entries.behaviour: Bits 4 to 0 enable the interrupt for status bits 0 to 4 (timer A, B, ADPCM-B end of sample, buffer ready, zero) unless masked at 0x110. Bit 7 mixes all six FM channels when set, only three when clear; reset 0x1F leaves channels 4 to 6 silent. ADPCM-B flags raise the interrupt only when the extended status is read.

entries.name: prescaler 6
entries.description: Selects the clock divider 6.
entries.behaviour: Selecting this address with the address port sets the FM clock divider to 6 at once; the data byte is not looked at. The SSG divider follows: 4 for FM divider 6, 2 for 3, 1 for 2.

entries.name: prescaler 3
entries.description: Selects the clock divider 3.
entries.behaviour: Selecting this address with the address port sets the FM clock divider to 3 at once; it takes effect only while the divider is 6, so from 2 go through 0x2D first. The SSG divider follows: 4 for FM divider 6, 2 for 3, 1 for 2.

entries.name: prescaler 2
entries.description: Selects the clock divider 2.
entries.behaviour: Selecting this address with the address port sets the FM clock divider to 2 at once; the data byte is not looked at. The SSG divider follows: 4 for FM divider 6, 2 for 3, 1 for 2.

entries.name: detune, multiple
entries.description: Detune and frequency multiple of one operator.
entries.behaviour: Bits 6 to 4 are the detune (0 to 7) and bits 3 to 0 the frequency multiple (0 to 15, where 0 means one half). Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4.

entries.name: total level
entries.description: Total level of one operator, its output attenuation.
entries.behaviour: Bits 6 to 0 are the total level (0 to 127, larger is quieter); bit 7 is ignored. Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4.

entries.name: key scale, attack
entries.description: Key scale rate and attack rate of one operator.
entries.behaviour: Bits 7 to 6 are the key scale rate (0 to 3) and bits 4 to 0 the attack rate (0 to 31); bit 5 is ignored. Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4.

entries.name: AM enable, decay rate
entries.description: AM enable and decay rate of one operator.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 lets the channel's LFO AM (0xB4 bits 5 to 4) add attenuation to this operator; bits 4 to 0 are the decay rate (0 to 31). Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4.

entries.name: sustain rate
entries.description: Sustain rate of one operator.
entries.behaviour: Bits 4 to 0 are the sustain rate (0 to 31); bits 7 to 5 are ignored. Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4.

entries.name: sustain level, release
entries.description: Sustain level and release rate of one operator.
entries.behaviour: Bits 7 to 4 are the sustain level (0 to 15; 15 counts as 31 on a 5-bit scale) and bits 3 to 0 the release rate (0 to 15). Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4.

entries.name: SSG-EG
entries.description: SSG-style envelope shape of one operator.
entries.behaviour: Bit 3 enables it; bits 2 to 0 are the shape: 0 repeat, 1 once and hold low, 2 repeat alternating, 3 once and hold high, 4 to 7 the same inverted. Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4.

entries.name: frequency low
entries.description: Low 8 bits of a channel's frequency number.
entries.behaviour: A write to offset 0 to 2 stores the byte and applies the block and high bits last written to 0xA4 to 0xA6, so write that register first. One latch serves all channels; offset 3 is ignored.

sources.cites: //        A0-A3 xxxxxxxx Frequency number lower 8 bits

against.line: //        A0-A3 xxxxxxxx Frequency number lower 8 bits

entries.name: block, frequency high
entries.description: Block and high 3 bits of a channel's frequency number, latched.
entries.behaviour: Bits 5 to 3 are the block (octave, 0 to 7) and bits 2 to 0 the frequency number bits 10 to 8; bits 7 to 6 are dropped. The write only fills a latch, which the next write to 0xA0 to 0xA2 applies to that channel; offset 3 is ignored.

entries.name: channel 2 freq low
entries.description: Low 8 bits of the frequency number of one operator of channel 2, in per-operator frequency mode.
entries.behaviour: Used only while 0x27 bits 7 to 6 are not 0: offset 0 is operator 3, offset 1 operator 1, offset 2 operator 2, and operator 4 keeps the channel's 0xA2 and 0xA6. A write applies the latch filled by 0xAC to 0xAE; offset 3 is ignored.

sources.cites: //        A8-AB xxxxxxxx Frequency number lower 8 bits

against.line: //        A8-AB xxxxxxxx Frequency number lower 8 bits

entries.name: channel 2 block, high
entries.description: Block and high 3 bits of the per-operator frequency of channel 2, latched.
entries.behaviour: Bits 5 to 3 are the block and bits 2 to 0 the frequency number bits 10 to 8, same offsets as 0xA8: 0 operator 3, 1 operator 1, 2 operator 2. A latch of its own, separate from the one of 0xA4, holds the value until 0xA8 to 0xAA is written. Offset 3 is ignored.

entries.name: feedback, algorithm
entries.description: Feedback of operator 1 and connection algorithm of a channel.
entries.behaviour: Bits 5 to 3 are the feedback of operator 1 (0 to 7) and bits 2 to 0 the algorithm (0 to 7); bits 7 to 6 are ignored. Bits 1 to 0 of the address pick the channel (0 to 2).

entries.name: pan, LFO sensitivity
entries.description: Output panning and LFO sensitivities of a channel.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 sends the channel to the left output and bit 6 to the right (both clear is silent); bits 5 to 4 are the AM sensitivity (0 to 3) and bits 2 to 0 the PM sensitivity (0 to 7). Reset value 0xC0.

entries.name: ID code
entries.description: The value a read of the data port returns after selecting address 0xFF.
entries.behaviour: Reading the data port after 0xFF has been written to the register select returns 1. A write there is stored in the FM block and unused.

entries.name: ADPCM-B control
entries.description: Starts, stops and configures the ADPCM-B playback channel.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 starts playback unless bit 0 is set, bit 6 records (unsupported: nothing plays while it is set), bit 5 reads samples from external memory, bit 4 repeats, bit 3 speaker is stored and unused, bit 0 resets and stops. Addresses are latched at the first fetch, so they may follow this byte.

entries.name: ADPCM-B pan, mode
entries.description: Output side and memory mode of the ADPCM-B channel.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 sends the output to the left and bit 6 to the right. Bits 1 and 0 (8-bit DRAM, ROM) make the address unit 32 bytes when either is set, else 4 bytes. Bits 3 and 2 (start conversion, DAC enable) are stored and unused.

entries.name: ADPCM-B start address
entries.description: Start address of the ADPCM-B sample.
entries.behaviour: 0x102 is the low byte and 0x103 the high byte, in the unit chosen at 0x101. It is used only with external memory (0x100 bit 5), is latched at the first fetch after a start, and is where a repeat restarts.

entries.name: ADPCM-B end address
entries.description: End address of the ADPCM-B sample.
entries.behaviour: 0x104 is the low byte and 0x105 the high byte, in the same unit. Playback ends after the last byte of the unit with that number and sets end-of-sample; with repeat set it restarts at the start address, else it stops. It is checked before the limit address.

entries.name: ADPCM-B prescale
entries.description: Prescale value of the ADPCM-B channel.
entries.behaviour: 0x106 is the low byte and 0x107 bits 2 to 0 the high bits. Stored and unused by MAME.

entries.name: ADPCM-B data read
entries.description: Reads the next byte of sample memory through the ADPCM-B channel.
entries.behaviour: Returns the next sample byte only while playback is off, record is off and external memory is on, advancing the address and setting buffer-ready; the first read returns the last value written to 0x108. Otherwise it returns 0, as does a read of any other register from 0x100 to 0x10F.

entries.name: ADPCM-B data write
entries.description: Data byte for CPU-fed playback or for recording into sample memory.
entries.behaviour: While playing with external and record clear, a write clears buffer-ready and the byte is taken at the next fetch. Stopped with external and record set, it stores the byte in sample memory and advances the address; stopped with external set and record clear, it acts as a dummy read.

entries.name: ADPCM-B delta-N
entries.description: Playback step of the ADPCM-B channel.
entries.behaviour: 0x109 is the low byte and 0x10A the high byte of a 16-bit step. Each FM sample period adds it to a 16-bit phase and a sample is decoded each time that overflows, so the playback rate is the step over 65536 of the FM sample rate; samples are linearly interpolated.

entries.name: ADPCM-B level
entries.description: Output gain of the ADPCM-B channel.
entries.behaviour: Each sample is multiplied by this byte and shifted down by 9 bits, so 0 is silent.

entries.name: ADPCM-B limit address
entries.description: Address at which external-memory playback wraps.
entries.behaviour: 0x10C is the low byte and 0x10D the high byte, in the unit of 0x101; reset value 0xFFFF. With external memory, finishing the unit with that number wraps the address to 0 with no status change; the end address wins when both match.

entries.name: ADPCM-B DAC, PCM data
entries.description: DAC data and PCM data of the ADPCM-B channel.
entries.behaviour: 0x10E is DAC data and 0x10F PCM data. Both are stored and unused by MAME.

entries.name: flag control
entries.description: Resets the status flags or chooses which ones are masked.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 set resets the timer flags and the ADPCM-B end-of-sample and playing flags and leaves the mask alone. Bit 7 clear stores bits 4 to 0 as a mask hiding the matching extended-status bits and blocking their interrupt (bit 0 timer A, 1 timer B, 2 end of sample, 3 buffer ready, 4 zero); reset value 0x1C.

entries.name: detune, multiple 2
entries.description: Detune and frequency multiple of one operator. Second bank.
entries.behaviour: Bits 6 to 4 are the detune (0 to 7) and bits 3 to 0 the frequency multiple (0 to 15, where 0 means one half). Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2, channels 3 to 5), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4. Second bank.

entries.name: total level 2
entries.description: Total level of one operator, its output attenuation. Second bank.
entries.behaviour: Bits 6 to 0 are the total level (0 to 127, larger is quieter); bit 7 is ignored. Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2, channels 3 to 5), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4. Second bank.

entries.name: key scale, attack 2
entries.description: Key scale rate and attack rate of one operator. Second bank.
entries.behaviour: Bits 7 to 6 are the key scale rate (0 to 3) and bits 4 to 0 the attack rate (0 to 31); bit 5 is ignored. Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2, channels 3 to 5), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4. Second bank.

entries.name: AM enable, decay rate 2
entries.description: AM enable and decay rate of one operator. Second bank.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 lets the channel's LFO AM (0xB4 bits 5 to 4) add attenuation to this operator; bits 4 to 0 are the decay rate (0 to 31). Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2, channels 3 to 5), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4. Second bank.

entries.name: sustain rate 2
entries.description: Sustain rate of one operator. Second bank.
entries.behaviour: Bits 4 to 0 are the sustain rate (0 to 31); bits 7 to 5 are ignored. Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2, channels 3 to 5), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4. Second bank.

entries.name: sustain level, release 2
entries.description: Sustain level and release rate of one operator. Second bank.
entries.behaviour: Bits 7 to 4 are the sustain level (0 to 15; 15 counts as 31 on a 5-bit scale) and bits 3 to 0 the release rate (0 to 15). Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2, channels 3 to 5), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4. Second bank.

entries.name: SSG-EG 2
entries.description: SSG-style envelope shape of one operator. Second bank.
entries.behaviour: Bit 3 enables it; bits 2 to 0 are the shape: 0 repeat, 1 once and hold low, 2 repeat alternating, 3 once and hold high, 4 to 7 the same inverted. Offset: bits 1 to 0 pick the channel (0 to 2, channels 3 to 5), then +0, +8, +4, +12 are operators 1, 2, 3, 4. Second bank.

entries.name: frequency low 2
entries.description: Low 8 bits of a channel's frequency number.
entries.behaviour: A write to offset 0 to 2 stores the byte and applies the block and high bits last written to 0x1A4 to 0x1A6, so write that register first. One latch serves all channels, shared with the first bank; offset 3 is ignored. Second bank.

sources.cites: //        A0-A3 xxxxxxxx Frequency number lower 8 bits

against.line: //        A0-A3 xxxxxxxx Frequency number lower 8 bits

entries.name: block, frequency high 2
entries.description: Block and high 3 bits of a channel's frequency number, latched.
entries.behaviour: Bits 5 to 3 are the block (octave, 0 to 7) and bits 2 to 0 the frequency number bits 10 to 8; bits 7 to 6 are dropped. The write only fills a latch, which the next write to 0x1A0 to 0x1A2 applies to that channel; offset 3 is ignored. Second bank.

entries.name: feedback, algorithm 2
entries.description: Feedback of operator 1 and connection algorithm of a channel.
entries.behaviour: Bits 5 to 3 are the feedback of operator 1 (0 to 7) and bits 2 to 0 the algorithm (0 to 7); bits 7 to 6 are ignored. Bits 1 to 0 of the address pick the channel (0 to 2, channels 3 to 5). Second bank.

entries.name: pan, LFO sensitivity 2
entries.description: Output panning and LFO sensitivities of a channel.
entries.behaviour: Bit 7 sends the channel to the left output and bit 6 to the right (both clear is silent); bits 5 to 4 are the AM sensitivity (0 to 3) and bits 2 to 0 the PM sensitivity (0 to 7). Reset value 0xC0. Second bank.
